ladder.name: Heating and hot water only
ladder.adds: The Phase A district on the standard two-tier tariff. The heat-pump tanks are the only flexible devices. An ideal controller saves 0.8 % of the yearly bill.

ladder.name: Assumed solar panels
ladder.adds: Rooftop solar on every building, sized from the building's own yearly use (south facing, tilted, pvlib model), and an assumed export price. Surplus sun can be stored in the tanks. An ideal controller saves 6.0 % of the year and 5.5 % of the eight test weeks.

ladder.name: Assumed solar panels and battery
ladder.adds: S1 plus a battery per building, one kilowatt-hour per kilowatt of solar, with assumed efficiency and power. An ideal controller saves 15.6 % of the year and 14.6 % of the eight test weeks.

ladder.name: Assumed solar, battery and building thermal model
ladder.adds: S2 plus a single-node model of each building's heat balance with a comfort band around the thermostat setpoint, so the walls can store heat; the thermostat is the reference. An ideal controller saves 16.0 % of the year and 14.7 % of the eight test weeks.

prose.intro: Phase A simulated heating and hot water only. Phase B adds solar panels, a battery, a building thermal model and richer prices, one rung at a time, and asks the same question at each rung: how much of the electricity bill could an ideal controller with perfect foresight save? Every solar size, battery size, export price and building parameter on this page is an assumption, not a measurement of these buildings.
prose.gate: The project rule is to add learning only where the exact optimum saves at least 3 % of the bill. The bare Phase A district (0.8 %) does not pass; S1, S2 and S3 do.
prose.ceilings: The saving is measured on the eight test weeks used for every controller and on the full year. The two differ a little because the test weeks are not a typical sample of the year.
prose.mass: Letting the building store heat in its own walls adds 1.6 percentage points on top of the tanks and the battery (S3 with a comfort band against S3 with the building held at the thermostat path). Under a wider comfort band the ceiling is 20.9 %.
prose.export: The export price matters most: the S2 ceiling is 22.2 % when exports earn nothing and 10.4 % at the highest price tested.
prose.tariffs: Richer price structures raise the ceilings: across all tariff variants, including the stylised ones, the S2 ceiling ranges from 15.6 % to 32.9 %. Pilot and day-ahead structures were applied outside the period they come from, and the stylised spreads are what-ifs, not tariffs that exist.
prose.resolution: Simulating in quarter-hours instead of hours changes the S2 ceiling by +0.6 percentage points; the weather stays hourly information.
prose.peaks: The bill-optimal schedule is not a grid-friendly schedule. On S2 the highest hour of the district rises from 72 kW to 125 kW (+74 %), on S3 by +96 %, because the battery and tanks all charge in the cheapest hours.
prose.evleg: Electric-vehicle charging and a local electricity community are labelled what-ifs on S2. Making the vehicles' charging flexible is worth 24 CHF a year (0.12 % of the bill); the community gain depends on the grid-fee discount assumed.
